subject: Civil Engineering
title: Prestressed Concrete: Built-In Squeeze
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Prestressed Concrete: Built-In Squeeze.

hook.text: Concrete cracks in tension. Engineers solved this by squeezing it before loading.

buildup.text: Steel cables are stretched tight inside the concrete, then released. They compress it.

discovery.text: When loads arrive, the tension they create must first overcome the built-in compression.

twist.text: Prestressed beams span much farther with less material than ordinary reinforced ones.

climax.text: Most highway bridge girders today are prestressed — lighter, longer, and crack-free.

punchline.text: Squeeze concrete first and it forgets how to crack.

quiz.question: How does prestressing prevent cracks in concrete?
options: It adds chemical additives that make concrete flexible
Steel cables compress the concrete so loads must overcome that squeeze first
It replaces concrete with a stronger polymer material

details.summary: Prestressed concrete applies permanent compressive force to concrete before service loads arrive. Pre-tensioning stretches steel strands before casting and transfers force when concrete hardens.
details.whyItMatters: Prestressing enables concrete to span much farther than ordinary reinforced concrete by eliminating tensile cracking under service loads. It makes possible precast parking garages, long-span bridges, and thin concrete shells.
takeaways: Pre-compression counteracts the tension that external loads will produce
Pre-tensioned strands are stressed before concrete is cast around them
Post-tensioned tendons are stressed after the concrete has hardened and cured

faq.question: How does prestressing allow concrete to span longer distances?
faq.answer: Under load, ordinary reinforced concrete cracks on the tension face, limiting usable span. Prestressing applies enough compression to ensure the tension face never actually goes into tension under service loads.

faq.question: What is the difference between pre-tensioning and post-tensioning?
faq.answer: Pre-tensioning stretches strands in a casting bed before concrete is poured. When the concrete hardens and strands are cut, prestress transfers through bond. Post-tensioning places strands in ducts within already-cast concrete, then stresses them with jacks and anchors them at the ends.
